archetype.name: Rebuilding (bottom of the league)
archetype.definition: A team in the league's basement for a second straight year, whose season is about sorting out the roster around Sabonis and a high-usage lead guard rather than about the standings.

report.headline: Not unlucky, just outclassed: a broken rim defense and a lost possession game
report.take:
Sacramento is 1-12 and 30th of 30 on the site, and nothing in the sheet says the record is lying. The Net Rtg of -13.4 ranks 29th. The W vs Pt Diff is only -1, and the margin implies just 2 wins, so this is not a decent team losing coin flips. It is last season's 22-60 team (-10.1 Net Rtg) with a worse offense. The ORtg has fallen from 111.4 to 107.4, while the 120.8 DRtg is barely better than last year's 121.5.

The defense is a paradox. Opponents take the smallest share of their shots at the rim of any team in the league (Opp Rim Rate 22.5, 1st), and the Kings clean up misses well (DRB % 74.4, 6th). But when shots do get to the basket, they go in 74.8% of the time. That is the worst mark in the league and 9.7 points above average, and it drags the Opp eFG % to 57.4, also last. Centers average 22.69 points against them (25th), which tells the same story: there is no deterrent inside. The offense has a different problem. The shooting is close to league average (eFG % 52.7 against 53.5), but the possession battle is lost. TOV % is 15.4 (27th), ORB % is 22.8 (28th) and FT Rate is 26.1 (23rd). On top of that, the ball runs through Darius Acuff Jr. at a 33 USG % and a 51.6 TS %, while the efficient scorers sit lower in the pecking order: Domantas Sabonis at 68.1 TS % on 16.5 usage, and Zach LaVine at 65.1.

Two things in the sheet look like trends but deserve a discount. November's defense (115.14 allowed a game) looks far better than October's 128.33. But the October run shown here was a road trip through San Antonio, New Orleans and Memphis, and the last five games, all at home, still gave up 118. The on-off numbers are mostly noise at this sample. Emanuel Sharp is +19.5 with a -6.2 BPM, and LaVine is -9.8 despite the second-best efficiency on the team. Nobody should build a rotation off those.

Where this goes depends on bodies. LaVine, De'Andre Hunter and Precious Achiuwa are all listed out, and the scoring has already sagged to 105.4 a game over the last five. The full-season pace of 6 wins is too grim; rim conversion that extreme should drift back toward normal. Still, every roster group grades D or worse (wings D-), and a bottom-three finish is the realistic shape of the season.

strengths.title: Sabonis is the one efficient engine
strengths.body: Sabonis is 15th of 92 on the center tab, with a 68.1 TS %, a 2.3 BPM and 1.2 Win Shares. His Win Shares are most of the frontcourt's 1.5 total, and the frontcourt is the only group producing meaningfully. He does it as a hub, with 67 assists, not as a volume scorer, which makes his efficiency repeatable. The issue is that the offense gives him only 16.5 USG %. The ceiling here is about allocation, not his level.

strengths.title: Shot profile and defensive boards hold
strengths.body: The Kings keep opponents out of the paint better than any team (Opp Rim Rate 22.5, 1st) and finish defensive possessions with the glass (DRB % 74.4, 6th). Both are structural habits rather than shooting luck, so they should last. If the rim finishing against them normalizes, this becomes a below-average defense rather than a catastrophic one.

concerns.title: No resistance once shots reach the rim
concerns.body: Opponents shoot 74.8% within four feet, the worst mark in the league and 9.7 above average. That is the main reason the Opp eFG % of 57.4 ranks last. Last season's figure was 69.8, so the weakness is real, though this year's level is extreme enough to come down some. With Achiuwa out, the backup center minutes are even thinner.

concerns.title: Possession game sinks the offense
concerns.body: The shooting is only slightly below league (eFG % gap -0.8), yet the ORtg sits 6.8 points under average. The difference is turnovers (TOV % 15.4, 27th), few second chances (ORB % 22.8, 28th) and few free throws. Acuff carrying a 33 USG % at a 51.6 TS % concentrates the problem in one player, and Malik Monk's 49.7 TS % off the bench does not offset it.

concerns.title: Injuries hollow out the rotation
concerns.body: LaVine, Hunter and Achiuwa are all listed out. LaVine is the team's best-rated guard (25th of 109) and its most efficient perimeter scorer. Scoring has slipped to 105.4 a game over the last five, below the season average. Until he returns, the wings (graded D-) lean on players like Alex Karaban, who sits last on his tab.

trend.note: The margin has barely moved: the last 10 games run at -13.1 a game against -13.46 for the season. The defense looks better in November, mostly on the schedule, while the offense has drifted down as injuries piled up.

weekAhead.headline: Phoenix is the opening; Lakers, Celtics and Spurs close it fast
weekAhead.body:
The week opens with the one winnable game, Phoenix at home. The Suns are 5-7 with a 119 DRtg (26th) and are the league's worst defensive rebounding team, and they get hit hard by point guards and centers. Then the schedule turns brutal: at the 12-2 Lakers (ORtg 123, 1st), then home against Boston (Net Rtg 13.7, 1st) and San Antonio (13, 2nd). The Spurs have already beaten Sacramento twice by wide margins this season.

Against the three contenders, the Kings' own weaknesses get exploited. The Lakers own the league's best eFG %, which punishes a defense that can't stop finishes. Boston and San Antonio both sit near 107 DRtg and protect the rim at a top-three level. The Spurs also turn it over less than anyone, so there are no cheap possessions to steal. Realistically, this week is about whether Phoenix can be taken and the rest kept respectable.

keyMatchups.title: Acuff against soft point-guard defenses
keyMatchups.body: Phoenix allows 32.92 points a game to point guards, the most in the league, and the Lakers are 29th at that spot. Acuff has the usage to exploit it. These two games are the best test all season of whether his efficiency can rise to match his volume. Boston, third-stingiest against point guards, is the opposite test.

keyMatchups.title: Sabonis on Phoenix's weak glass
keyMatchups.body: The Suns rank last in DRB % and 29th in points allowed to centers. That gives Sabonis a rare chance to lift the Kings' 28th-ranked offensive rebounding and score inside. San Antonio also gives centers more than their usual output. Boston allows centers only 15.31 a game, fifth-fewest.

keyMatchups.title: Spurs rematch, third time
keyMatchups.body: Sacramento lost 103-130 in San Antonio and 109-124 at home. The Spurs lead the league in RPG and in ball security (TOV % 10.7), which removes the two areas where the Kings' defense shows any life. A third lopsided result is the likeliest outcome.

weekAhead.watch: Whether Acuff turns the two softest point-guard defenses in the league (Phoenix, then the Lakers) into an efficient night, rather than just a high-volume one.

restOfSeason.body:
The full-season pace of 6 wins overstates the collapse. Opponents finishing at 74.8% around the rim is an outlier even for a weak defense, and LaVine's return would restore the one perimeter scorer who is efficient at volume. Neither fix touches the structure, though. The turnovers, the absent offensive rebounding and the D grades across every group look like a roster that finishes in the league's bottom three. I project 13 to 20 wins, with the Net Rtg settling between -12.5 and -8.5, roughly last season's level, as the rim defense normalizes.

What is sustainable is the defensive rebounding and the shot-profile defense. What will regress, in Sacramento's favor, is the rim finishing against it. The swing is on offense. If Acuff's efficiency doesn't rise, a 33% usage share keeps the ORtg near the league's floor no matter who returns.
swingFactors: Rim FG% allowed drifting toward league average

confidence.note: Only 13 games, but the margin matches last season's, and the record lines up with the point differential.
